submitted.rationale: Index 69 (Bi0.07 Cu0.54 V0.39), near Cu3V2O8 stoichiometry, had the highest measured photocurrent: 6.2e-7 A. Cu-vanadate phases absorb 2.4 eV photons better than the BiVO4/V2O5-rich region. Going further toward Cu-rich, CuO-dominated compositions reduced the photocurrent.

rejected.reason: BiVO4 + CuV2O6 region gave only 1.6e-7 A; absorption is marginal at 2.4 eV.
The Cu-rich, CuO-dominated film gave 1.8e-7 A; CuO is p-type and a poor photoanode.

consultations.verdict: Weak support. V2O5 and Bi2O3 are stable end-members (on hull); V2O5's predicted gap is 2.83 eV, which is above the 2.4 eV photon energy, so the V-rich/Bi region needs BiVO4/Cu-vanadate phases to absorb. Index 0 (Bi0.24 Cu0.18 V0.58) sits near a BiVO4 + CuV2O6 mixture, the canonical photoanode region. Measure as a baseline.

Mixed support. MEGNet gives CuO a small gap (0.32 eV), so Cu adds visible absorption; mixed Cu vanadates (Cu3V2O8, Cu2V2O7, about 2 eV in the literature) should absorb 2.4 eV photons well, unlike the V2O5/BiVO4-rich region. Index 69 (Cu0.54 V0.39 Bi0.07) is near Cu3V2O8 stoichiometry, so it explores a region distinct from index 0.

Uninformative to weak support. CuO is essentially on the hull (0.001 eV/atom), so the Cu-rich region will be CuO plus a Cu vanadate that absorbs strongly. The measured trend (index 0: 1.6e-7 A, index 69: 6.2e-7 A) rises with Cu. Index 78 (Cu0.78 V0.12 Bi0.10) extends that direction and is a deliberate exploratory bet.
